headline: Compelling valuation at ~$1.8M market cap — below 50% of current sales, less than 4x book value of rental fleet, trading at a discount to PP&E — with rental momentum building and ambitious fleet growth plans over 18 months
reasoning: Richard Jenkins argues the company is deeply undervalued with a market cap of approximately $1.8 million, which is less than 50% of current annual sales and less than four times the book value of its existing rental fleet. The company is also trading at a discount to the value of its property, plant and equipment. A one-for-one non-renounceable rights issue raising ~$1.69 million is underway, with more than 50% of proceeds earmarked to fulfil existing rental pallet contracts and maintain commercial momentum. The company has a pipeline of clients for whom it has designed exclusive pallets, and is in advanced discussions with bank and non-bank funding partners to scale the rental business further. Management has stripped costs aggressively, including head office redundancies, to preserve cash for the rental growth strategy.
quote: Well, look, the valuation of this company is incredibly cheap. We're value, our market cap is we're a micro, micro cap company. Our valuation is approximately $1.8 million, which is less than 50% of our current sales. It's not even four times the value of the book value of our rental fleet as it stands now. And we have very, very ambitious plans for that to grow substantially in the next 18 months. We're trading at a discount to the value of our PP and E, so the valuation metrics are compelling.
episode_title: Range International bets on pallet rentals

headline: Rental pallets dominate internationally because customers prefer OpEx over CapEx, but Indonesian rental market is competitive with well-capitalised incumbents Chep and Loscom posing significant challenges
reasoning: Jenkins notes that the majority of the global pallet market is characterised by rental rather than outright purchase, as companies prefer to use OpEx budgets and preserve CapEx for other purposes. However, the Indonesian rental market is competitive, with major incumbents Chep and Loscom holding well-established pooling infrastructure and strong financial backing, making it critical for Range to secure funding partnerships to scale its rental fleet and compete effectively.
quote: The majority of the pallet market internationally is characterised by a heavy emphasis on rentals because many companies wish to preserve CapEx for other purposes and use the pallet purchases out of their OpEx budget, which means that the rental is an obvious way for them to go... Our major competitors in the rental space are Chip and Loscom. So that makes it especially challenging for us because they have very well established pooling facilities and also they have tremendous financial backbone.
episode_title: Range International bets on pallet rentals
